metadata.title: Exact Non-Perturbative Spectral Mass Gap, Complete Glueball Spectrum, and Center Vortex Condensation for 4D SU(3) Yang-Mills Theory on Foliated Voronoi-Delaunay Complexes in Unified Phase Dynamics
metadata.description:
We construct a non-perturbative mathematical framework establishing the rigorous existence of quantum Yang–Mills theory with compact gauge group G = SU(3) on flat spacetime ℝ4 and derive a strictly positive spectral mass gap Δ > 0 within the Unified Phase Dynamics of Feynman Path Contours.

Classical hypercubic lattices ℤ4 break continuous SO(4) rotational invariance down to the discrete hypercubic subgroup H(4), producing O(a2) dimension-6 Symanzik artifacts, while higher-derivative continuum regulators encounter the Schoenberg–Bochner obstruction and Ostrogradsky ghost poles that violate reflection positivity. In this work, taking the flat-spacetime decoupling limit G → 0 (Rμναβ ≡ 0) of the universal path-contour master-functional Ψ[Σ], the gauge-invariant Wilson loop holonomies project onto a foliated four-dimensional cellular complex 𝒞a = 𝒱a(3) × aτℤ1/2. Each spatial slice is a three-dimensional Poisson–Delaunay triangulation with exact analytical mean coordination number ⟨z3D⟨ = 48π2/35 + 2 ≈ 15.5355, endowed with Discrete Exterior Calculus (DEC) Hodge star coupling weights.

Key mathematical and physical achievements:

  • Strict Reflection Positivity (OS2): Discrete time slicing with step aτ/2 and spatial reflection symmetry preserve strict Osterwalder–Seiler reflection positivity at every finite lattice spacing a > 0, allowing GNS reconstruction of a positive-definite physical Hilbert space with self-adjoint Hamiltonian H ≥ 0 without ghosts.
  • Restoration of Continuous SO(4) Invariance (OS1): Ensemble averaging over random Poisson Delaunay seeds restores exact statistical isotropy ⟨pμpνpρpσ⟩ ∝ δ(μνδρσ), eliminating cubic lattice artifacts in the continuum limit.
  • Rigorous Two-Sided Bounds on the Mass Gap: Combining the Glimm–Jaffe–Simon chessboard estimate with the Borel–Chebyshev inequality and Rayleigh–Ritz variational flux-tube minimization proves the two-sided bounds cgeom√σ ≤ Δ0++ ≤ 2√π√σ ≈ 1.56–1.62 GeV, and Δ0++ ≈ 1.65 GeV including the Lüscher Casimir term, matching continuum Lattice QCD (1.65 ± 0.10 GeV).
  • Steiner Tree Baryon Relaxation: 3-quark string Y-junctions relax to the Torricelli angle 119.98° ± 1.81° (exact 120° continuum limit) and conserve ℤ3 center triality (1 + 1 + 1 ≡ 0 mod 3).
